content:
iPhone Ultra will be released next month, and a new leak suggests the front camera on this device may be positioned in an unusual location.

The two front cameras on the iPhone Ultra may no longer be centred, but instead placed at two corners respectively.

When the iPhone Ultra launches, it will be Apple's first attempt at a foldable iPhone. As a result, the device will differ from the design of a 'normal' iPhone in several aspects, including the camera layout.

The iPhone Ultra is rumoured to feature two rear cameras — a main lens and an ultra-wide lens — along with two front cameras.

The reason for having two front cameras is that the foldable device will have two screens: one on the outside, and a larger screen that is only revealed when unfolded.

Until now, we had expected the front camera on the outer screen to be placed in the centre. However, according to a new leak, the camera placement may be even more unconventional.

A third-party screen protector circulating online appears to show a camera cut-out at the top-right corner of the outer screen and another at the top-left corner of the inner screen.

Accessory manufacturers may well have got it wrong. Like everyone else, they are only working from speculation. But if this leak turns out to be true, it would mark a significant departure from previous front camera placements.

Apple has always positioned the selfie camera at the top-centre of the iPhone. If it were moved to a corner, users might look at the wrong lens in many selfies (especially group selfies).

Shifting the inner screen's camera off-centre makes more sense. After all, the camera cannot be placed right in the middle of the hinge, and selfies will typically be taken using the outer screen anyway. However, if even the outer screen's camera is not centred, users will need time to readjust.

If Apple really does move the iPhone Ultra's front camera to a corner, do you think it's a problem? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
